title: What If the Siberian Traps Erupted Again?

scenes.text: What if the volcano that nearly ended life on Earth erupted again? It wasn't one volcano.
About 250 million years ago, lava in Siberia spread across roughly 7 million square kilometers, enough to cover Australia.
It kept erupting for hundreds of thousands of years, pumping out huge amounts of warming gases.
Acid rain fell, at times making the ground as acidic as lemon juice.
Over roughly 60,000 years, about 90 percent of marine species and most land species died out.
It is called the Great Dying, the worst mass extinction we know of, and it happened slowly.

description:
What if the Siberian Traps erupted again?
About 250 million years ago, floods of lava and gas helped wipe out roughly 90 percent of ocean species.
What should we run through next?
